security_audit.summary: The seven external command detections are false positives from Markdown fences and inline skill names, not executable shell or Ruby syntax. One semantic concern remains: the database tool example directly executes agent-supplied SQL and should include safety controls.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the direct SQL execution example with parameterized read-only queries, operation allow-lists, and explicit approval before database access.

content.value_statement: Designing multi-agent systems requires clear roles, tasks, tools, and process choices. This skill guides CrewAI planning, implementation, and review for Python workflows.
actual_capabilities: Designs CrewAI agents with roles, goals, backstories, and tool assignments.
Defines tasks with dependencies, expected outputs, and context sharing.
Chooses sequential, hierarchical, or flow-based orchestration patterns.
Explains CrewAI memory options and custom storage integration points.
Shows how to add custom tools to agents with scoped responsibilities.
Combines CrewAI with related observability and structured output skills.
limitations: It assumes Python and basic multi-agent concepts.
It does not validate code against your local runtime or APIs.
It cannot provide credentials or configure live external services.
Simple tasks may not need a multi-agent design.

use_cases.title: Plan an Agent Team
use_cases.description: Create a CrewAI design with clear roles, tasks, process type, inputs, and expected outputs.

use_cases.title: Review Orchestration Choices
use_cases.description: Compare sequential, hierarchical, and flow-based designs for a specific workflow.

use_cases.title: Add Tools and Memory
use_cases.description: Scope agent tools, memory, and integrations before building a production workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Explain CrewAI Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this CrewAI skill to explain whether my task needs agents, tasks, crews, and processes. My task is: {task}.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Basic Crew
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CrewAI crew for {goal}. Include agent roles, task order, expected outputs, process type, and required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CrewAI design for role clarity, task dependencies, process choice, memory use, and tool scope: {design}.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a CrewAI Flow for {workflow}. Include state, routing decisions, crew boundaries, failure handling, observability, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Create a research and writing crew for a product launch brief.
output_examples.output: A plan with researcher and writer agents, sequenced tasks, expected outputs, required inputs, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Review my CrewAI flow for a content pipeline.
output_examples.output: A review covering flow steps, routing choices, state handling, tool boundaries, and missing tests.

output_examples.input: Add memory and tools to an agent team.
output_examples.output: Guidance for memory scope, tool permissions, integration points, and safeguards before production use.

best_practices: Start with clear roles, goals, and expected outputs before adding tools or memory.
Use sequential processes until coordination needs justify hierarchical management or flows.
Restrict tools to the minimum permissions needed by each agent.
anti_patterns: Do not give every agent broad tools when only one task needs them.
Do not use multi-agent orchestration for simple single-step prompts.
Do not skip tests around tools, memory, and external integrations.

faq.question: Does this skill run CrewAI code?
faq.answer: No. It guides design and review. You still run, test, and secure code in your environment.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with YAML configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers agent and task configuration patterns commonly used in CrewAI projects.

faq.question: Does it cover CrewAI Flows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for event-driven flows, state, routing, and crew boundaries.

faq.question: Can it design custom tools?
faq.answer: Yes. Tool designs should use narrow permissions, validation, and approvals for sensitive actions.

faq.question: Is it only for Python projects?
faq.answer: Yes. CrewAI is a Python framework, and the examples assume Python project structure.
